A.subject: Physics
A.text: For a positively charged particle moving in a x-y plane initially along the x-axis, there is a sudden change in its path due to the presence of electric and/or magnetic fields beyond P. The curved path is found to be (for a brief time interval) in the x-y plane and is found to be non-circular. Which one of the following combinations is possible
options: vec(E) = 0; vec(B) = b î + c k̂
vec(E) = a î; vec(B) = c k̂ + a î
vec(E) = 0; vec(B) = c ĵ + b k̂
vec(E) = a î; vec(B) = c k̂ + b ĵ
A.sol_text:
Answer: (2)
Solution:
Electric field can deviate the path of the particle in the shown direction only when it is along negative y-direction. In the given options, vec(E) is either zero or along x-direction. Hence it is the magnetic field which is really responsible for its curved path. Options (a) and (c) can't be accepted as the path will be helix in that case (when the velocity vector makes an angle other than 0°, 180° or 90° with the magnetic field, path is a helix) option (d) is wrong because in that case component of net force on the particle also comes in k direction which is not acceptable as the particle is moving in x-y plane. Only in option (b) the particle can move in x-y plane.

In option (d): vec(F)_net = q vec(E) + q(vec(v) × vec(B))

Initial velocity is along x-direction. So let vec(v) = v î

∴ vec(F)_net = qa î + q[(v î) × (c k̂ + b ĵ)] = qa î − qvc ĵ + qvb k̂ □

In option (b): vec(F)_net = q(a î) + q[(v î) × (c k̂ + a î)] = qa î − qvc ĵ

B.text: The circuit shown in the diagram extends to infinity. Each resistance is equal to R = 8(√5 − 1) Ω. Find the effective resistance (in Ω) between terminal A and B.
B.sol_text:

R₀ = 2R + (2RR₀)/(2R + R₀)

Solution:
Equivalent circuit will be like.

Let R₀ is the equivalent resistance. Then,

(2RR₀)/(2R + R₀) + 2R = R₀

⇒ 2RR₀ + 4R² + 2RR₀ = 2RR₀ + R₀²

⇒ R₀² − 2RR₀ − 4R² = 0

⇒ R₀ = R(√5 + 1) ∴ R_eq = 8(√5 − 1)(√5 + 1)

⇒ R_eq = 32 Ω

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: A solution of 10 g of a non-volatile binary electrolyte (M.wt = 50) in 1000 g of water freezes at −0.74°C. What is the degree of dissociation of electrolyte? (K_f water = 1.85 K. molality^−1)
A.sol_text:
ΔT_f = K_f × molality × i

(T_f^0 − T_f^s) = K_f × (w.t of solute)/(M.wt of solute) × 1000/(wt of solvent) × i

0 − (−0.74) = 0.74 = 1.85 × (10/50) × (1000/1000) × i

i = (0.74 × 5)/(1.85) = 2

i = 1+ (n −1)α (Binary electrolyte n = 2)

2 = 1 + (2 − 1)α = 1 + α

α = 2 − 1 = 1

∴ Degree of dissociation = 100%

N₂O, N₂O₅, P₄O₆, P₄O₇, H₄P₂O₅, H₅P₃O₁₀, H₂S₂O₃, H₂S₂O₅
B.sol_text:
Answer: 05.00
Solution:

N₂O
N=N—O ⇌ N≡N⁺—O⁻
(No bridging oxo group)

N₂O₅
O=N—O—N=O (with structure showing bridging oxygen)
(Has bridging oxo group)

P₄O₆
(Structure showing P atoms connected by bridging oxygen atoms)
(Has bridging oxo group)

P₄O₇
(Structure showing P atoms connected by bridging oxygen atoms)
(Has bridging oxo group)

H₄P₂O₅
HO—P(=O)—O—P(=O)—OH (with H atoms)
(Has bridging oxo group)

H₅P₃O₁₀
HO—P(=O)(OH)—O—P(=O)(OH)—O—P(=O)(OH)—OH
(Has bridging oxo group)

H₂S₂O₃
HO—S(=O)—O—H
(No bridging oxo group - has S-O-H, not bridging O)

H₂S₂O₅
HO—S(=O)—S(=O)—OH
(Has bridging oxo group - S-O-S)

Total compounds with at least one bridging oxo group = 5
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If cos⁻¹(x/a) + cos⁻¹(y/b) = θ, then the value of √(x²/a² + y²/b² - 2xy/(ab)cos θ) is equal to
A.sol_text:
Answer: (1)
Solution:

cos⁻¹(x/a) + cos⁻¹(y/b) = θ

Take cos both side
cos(A + B) = cos θ

Where cos A = x/a, sin A = √(1-x²)/a²

cos B = y/b, sin B = √(1-y²)/b²

⇒ (x/a)·(y/b) - √(a²-x²)/a·√(b²-y²)/b = cos θ

⇒ xy/(ab) - √((a²-x²)(b²-y²))/(ab) = cos θ

⇒ xy/(ab) - cos θ = √(1 - y²/b² - x²/a² + x²y²/(a²b²))

(square both side)

⇒ x²y²/(a²b²) + cos² θ - 2xy/(ab)cos θ = 1 - x²/a² - y²/b² + x²y²/(a²b²)

⇒ x²/a² + y²/b² - 2xy/(ab)cos θ = 1 - cos² θ

Now taking square root

⇒ √(x²/a² + y²/b² - 2xy/(ab)cos θ) = |sin θ|

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: If the tangent at (x₁, y₁) to the curve x³ + y³ = a³ meets the curve again at (x₂, y₂), then |x₂/x₁ + y₂/y₁| is
B.sol_text:
Answer: 01.00
Solution:
The equation of the tangent to the given curve at (x₁, y₁) is given by

y - y₁ = -(3x₁²)/(3y₁²) (x - x₁)
⟹ x₁²x + y₁²y = x₁³ + y₁³ = a³
which meets the curve again at (x₂, y₂)
∴ x₁²x₂ + y₁²y₂ = a³ = x₁³ + y₁³ = x₂³ + y₂³
⟹ x₁²(x₂ - x₁) + y₁²(y₂ - y₁) = 0 and x₂(x₂² - x₁²) + y₂(y₂² - y₁²) = 0
Dividing them
x₂(x₁ + x₂)/(x₁²) - y₂(y₁ + y₂)/(y₁²) = 0

x₂/x₁ + x₂²/x₁² - y₂/y₁ - y₂²/y₁² = 0
⟹ (x₂/x₁ - y₂/y₁) + (x₂/x₁ - y₂/y₁)(x₂/x₁ + y₂/y₁) = 0
⟹ (x₂/x₁ - y₂/y₁)(x₂/x₁ + y₂/y₁ + 1) = 0
⟹ x₂/x₁ + y₂/y₁ = -1 as x₂/x₁ ≠ y₂/y₁
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: The trace of a square matrix is defined to be the sum of its diagonal entries. If A is a 2 × 2 matrix such that the trace of A is 3 and the trace of A³ is −18, then the value of the determinant of A is
B.sol_text:
Let A = [x y; z 3−x] ⇒ |A| = 3x − x² − yz

Now A² = [x y; z 3−x] · [x y; z 3−x]

= [x² + yz, xy + 3y − xy; 2x + 3z − xz, yz + 9 + x² − 6x] = [x² + yz, 3y; 3z, yz + 9 + x² − 6x]

⇒ A³ = [x² + yz, 3y; 3z, yz + 9 + x² − 6x] · [x y; z 3−x]

= [x³ + xyz + 3yz, x²y + y²z + 9y − 3xy; 3xz + yz² + 9z + x²z − 6xz, 6yz + 27 + 3x² − 18x − xyz − 9x − x³ + 6x²]

⇒ Trace = x³ + xyz + 3yz + 6yz + 27 + 3x² − 18x − xyz − 9x − x³ + 6x² = −18

⇒ 9yz + 9x² − 27x + 27 = −18

⇒ yz + x² − 3x + 3 = −2

x² − 3x + yz = −5

⇒ 3x − x² − yz = 5

|A| = 5
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
